question: Ascent DEF, you hold B at 2 (Killjoy). Your Alarmbot pings 1 ATK Mid Top, your A teammate says A Main is quiet. ATK grabbed Mid. How do you call it?

options.label: Stay on B with your setup, prep a short rotate: Mid control threatens B via Market as much as A via Catwalk
options.explication_courte: ATK Mid control opens a fast B split (via Market) as much as an A hit (Catwalk). Holding B with your Killjoy setup keeps the intel and the site covered.

options.label: Rotate early toward A to back up your solo A teammate, reading the Mid take as a Catwalk hit incoming
options.explication_courte: Mid control often feeds a Catwalk hit on A; reinforcing a solo teammate is defensible, but you abandon B and your Killjoy setup for an unconfirmed read.

sources_option.citation: Whoever controls mid gets better rotation timing and can split onto a site; if you lose mid, rotations must be earlier to avoid being punished.

options.label: Push Mid with your B teammate to contest the ATK and reclaim Mid control
options.explication_courte: Pushing Mid 2v4 abandons your site and engages on ATK-controlled ground; in a 4v4 you risk losing both Mid and B in one play.

sources_option.citation: Retaking lost mid control mid-round commits bodies into enemy-held space; defenders usually hold sites and let mid control funnel into a readable hit.

options.label: Dump Alarmbot + Nanoswarm into Mid immediately to deny their control, burn all setup now
options.explication_courte: Wasting your Killjoy setup in Mid before any hit lands leaves your site undefended when the split arrives - the setup is worthless away from a plant spot.

sources_option.citation: Use utility reactively and layer it; dumping your setup util early leaves you with nothing for the actual site hit.

explication_longue:
Situation: Ascent, you defend B at 2 (you Killjoy with setup + one B teammate), third teammate on A, fourth is down (4v4). Alarmbot or team callout pings 1 ATK Mid Top; A Main is quiet.

Key rotation principle: holding your site with intel beats rotating on an unconfirmed signal. On Ascent, ATK Mid control is ambiguous - it opens a B split via Market just as much as an A hit via Catwalk. Your Killjoy setup is your most powerful defensive asset; abandoning it for an early A rotate removes that for an unconfirmed threat.

The correct line: stay B, keep setup active, let the round develop. If the Mid ATK commits to A via Catwalk, your A teammate calls it and you make an informed rotate through Mid or CT. Early A rotate (acceptable) is defensible if your read on Catwalk is strong, but burns B. Pushing Mid in 2 (costly) fights on ATK-controlled ground. Dumping setup into Mid (mistake) wastes every defensive piece in the wrong location.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% hold B + conditional rotate, ~23% early A rotate, ~17% Mid push (costly), ~4% dump setup (mistake).

sources.citation: Whoever controls mid gets better rotation timing and split options; a mid take threatens multiple sites, and losing mid means rotating earlier.
A quiet site (zero signal) plus mid pressure usually means the hit is being set up through mid; read the split rather than committing on assumption.
Hold your site setup and let mid control funnel into a readable hit rather than committing bodies to retake lost mid space.

_gaps.incertitude: Le choix tenir-B vs rotate-A depend fortement de la meta de la map et du fait que sur Ascent un mid-take alimente historiquement plus A (Catwalk) que B (Market) selon certains coachs. La separation optimal/acceptable est la plus fine des 10 puzzles et devra etre tranchee par un juge Immortal+.
Un seul ATK est pinge Mid Top ; les 3 autres sont inconnus. Si un juge estime que le mid-control Ascent annonce majoritairement A, l'option 1 (rotate A) pourrait etre reclassee optimal.
Estimations depuis guides map-control/rotation (guildorder, bo3, boostroom) ; aucune donnee statistique sur la destination des splits post-mid-control par map en elite.
